blocks.text: MANAGEMENT SUBMISSION - AI ADOPTION AND PRODUCTIVITY IN SAP ABAP DELIVERY
SAP ABAP AI Utilisation, Productivity Improvement & Delivery Efficiency Report
Projects: PAL | ONGC (OVL) | T&G  -  Period 20 July - 19 November 2026  -  Arnav Johri, Associate Consultant (SAP ABAP), Diligent Global  -  AI tool: Claude Code (Anthropic)
1. Executive Summary

AI was part of my daily SAP ABAP work on three projects at the same time. I completed 74 AI-assisted developments: 51 for ONGC, 12 for T&G, 6 for PAL and 5 common tools. They include full applications (CDS / RAP dashboards, an approval workflow, forecasting), reports, interfaces, enhancements, ATC remediation of 51 program includes and root-cause analysis of production issues.

I worked 58 active days in the repository period, including 6 weekend days. On 6 days the work ran 8 hours or more from the first commit to the last, and the busiest day (22/10/26) had 68 commits, work from 09:37 to 22:08 IST (12.5 h). Output: 150,384 lines of code, 312 custom objects and 17 technical specifications.

**Strongest example:** ONGC Videsh JIB Status management dashboard. Eight CDS views and an analytical cube went from requirement (03/11/26) to written client confirmation (17/11/26) in 11 working days, at 50% less effort.

items: Every object folder of my work repository, with its issue log (issue, cause, fix) and technical notes; git history of all branches (869 commits).
Claude Code session records (30 sessions, 557 prompts, 20/07 - 15/08/26), the August OVL work log, ATC exports and handover, FS / TS documents and client feedback.

blocks.text: 6. ATC Correction and Code Optimisation Summary

rows: Findings routed for senior / functional decision

blocks.text: Finding types: SELECT SINGLE without a unique key, field-length extension, simplified objects (BSEG, KONV, VBUK / VBUP, J_1IMOVEND), CLIENT SPECIFIED on compatibility views, strict Open SQL. Optimisation beyond ATC: FOR ALL ENTRIES replaced by ranges where it lost rows, batch input on dead S/4 transactions replaced by BAPIs, aggregation moved to the database.
7. Automation and Reusable Development Summary

17 automations and tools. For users: daily BP-creation mail, mass uploads (forecast, exceptional approval, timesheet rows, JV alignment), the credit-memo approval workflow and period-end bank revaluation. For developers: source mass download, enhancement finder, ICF URL list, ST05 trace decoder and the AI delivery toolkit (7 workflow skills, 56 recorded release constraints, 76 ATC patterns).
8. Quantified Effort and Productivity Analysis

Effort without AI comes from a conservative baseline by work type and complexity. Actual effort with AI counts all my working time in the period, weekends included, spread over the developments by measured session time and size. Saved = without minus with; man-days = saved / 8. The workings are in the Excel register.
9. Customer Benefits

items: Capacity released to carry three projects in parallel, alongside production support.
Earlier testing: most developments reached a first working version within a working day.
Reusable assets for the team: ATC patterns, release constraints, forecast engine, workflow and analytical-cube patterns, developer tools.

blocks.text: 10. Overall Conclusions

items: AI is now part of how I deliver: faster first builds and faster root-cause analysis, with every object reviewed, activated and tested by me before go-live.
Next steps: share the AI delivery toolkit with the team, reuse the dashboard pattern for further cards, and apply the ATC patterns to the next remediation wave.
